event: 2014 regular season Week 5, Pittsburgh at Jacksonville, October 5, 2014
frozen: 2014-10-04, after the Saturday walkthrough of the thirty opening numbers with its short-yardage, backed-up and sudden-change interruptions, the substitutions, sideline signals and emergency calls, the Kelce and Nicks rechecks, the final medical and 46 check and Stone's freeze checklist; before any draw
provenance: Stone's Week 5 packet of September 28, 2014 (career/2014/05_Regular_Season/Games/Week_05/Week_05_Pittsburgh.md: the direction, the personnel and staff decisions, the Pittsburgh questions, the practice week and scripted periods, the thirty-call opening menu, the situational offense, the special-play cards, the sixteen defensive responses and the game operation and freeze), issued by Stone and applied September 29 to October 4. Every call below is a Week 4 frozen call from the active 2013 offensive book (Iteration I), carried as the packet names it. The packet numbers 30 opening calls: 18 distinct calls with the packet's numbering in 'opener' and twelve returns to a picture already shown in 'opener_returns', position 26 now the return to 12 SHIFT Empty Stick in place of last week's vacant number. The Trey TE Delay, Spacing from Doubles (two-minute and PRESS only) and Snag (low red zone and two-point only) complete 21 distinct calls; 12 Trey Y-Cross HALF is not carried and the Throwback Screen Left is on no folder (notes). The K and N player combinations were released on the week's unprompted checks (career/2014/05_Regular_Season/Games/Week_05/output.md, section 1). The label stream reads each call's menus, opener position and returns (kernel 2014.5); the returns, conditions, triggers, gates and alerts remain in-game coaching guidance the kernel does not condition on, and none of these fields enters the outcome packet. decisions carries Stone's standing two-point and onside rules verbatim; fourth downs are his live calls. defensive_call_sheet transcribes the sixteen defensive responses as a record only.

menus.opening_sequence: Stone's order as the packet numbers it: 12 Ace Power Right (1); 12 SHIFT Empty Stick (2); 12 Trey Y-Cross SOLID (3, C/K); 11 Bunch Mesh HALF (4, C/K); 12 Wing Outside Zone Left (5, the backside edge and pursuit recorded before 6); 12 Wing Boot Flood Right (6, only after a confirmed backside chase); the returns to 1 (7) and 2 (8); 12 Ace Counter Right (9); 11 Doubles Drive HALF (10, C/N); the return to 3 (11); 11 Doubles Stick SCAT (12, C/K/N); 11 Doubles RB Slow Screen (13, only against a credible rush); 12 Ace Power Left (14); the return to 4 (15); 12 Ace Flea Flicker MAX (16, only after the actual safety response supports the shot); 12 Wing TE Delay (17, only against a credible rush and a viable release lane); 11 SHIFT Empty Spacing SCAT (18); 11 Doubles Inside Zone Right (19, favorable structure only); the returns to 5 (20), 6 (21) and 3 (22); 11 Trips Inside Zone + Bubble (23, the taught count only); 12 Ace Power Pass / Post-Cross MAX (24, on its trigger); the returns to 9 (25) and 2 (26, the complete call that replaces last week's vacant number); 11 Trey Dagger HALF (27, eligible downs and clean protection only); the returns to 1 (28), 4 (29) and 3 (30). Eighteen distinct calls and twelve planned returns. A numbered opener is an eligible option, not a command to ignore down, distance, field position or coverage: Tice skips an ineligible item and retains it for a later suitable situation, and backed-up, third and fourth down, scoring and clock situations take precedence. Call control, unchanged from Week 4 with Stone calling both sides: Tice tracks the next eligible opener number and the situation folder and is the single offensive situation and opener relay; Bates supplies quarterback and protection information without issuing a competing call; Crennel prepares and transmits the defensive call; Skalaski brings the next clock, fourth-down and challenge decision early; Westhoff supplies the kicking information; Stone makes every call and every decision. If radio communication fails, the existing practiced sideline procedure and reduced menu apply.
menus.normal_down: first-and-10: Power, Counter, Outside Zone, Stick, the SOLID Y-Cross and Mesh according to the front, with the Dagger eligible behind clean protection; second-and-1-to-3: the lead-back run, the conditional Power Pass, and the Flea Flicker only when its setup is present; second-and-4-to-6: the Dagger's eligible window with the same normal-down calls; Jones-Drew is the back unless an identified relief call sends Anderson; tight-end receiving emphasis without a target quota, coverage deciding the throw
menus.second_and_long: the SOLID Y-Cross, Mesh HALF, Drive HALF, the RB Slow Screen, or Lewis's TE Delay from Wing or Trey; protection set first; the screen and the delay only with their rush reason
menus.third_down: third-and-1-2: Power, Counter, Mesh or the taught Inside Zone + Bubble count, no Dagger, the quick alternative only if it actually gains the needed yardage; third-and-3-5: Stick SCAT, Mesh HALF and Drive HALF, the immediate throw identified against the extra rusher and the sticks located; third-and-6-9: the SOLID Y-Cross, Drive HALF, the protected Dagger only with its gate satisfied, or the Slow Screen against the appropriate rush, no extra receiver released by leaving a rusher unaccounted; third-and-10-or-more: the same protected intermediate menu, with route depth and catch-and-run opportunity fitted to the distance
menus.backed_up: Power, Inside Zone, Outside Zone and Stick SCAT with a known pressure answer; no flea flicker, no throwback and no slow shot
menus.fourth_down: Stone's live call: the matching distance folder, and Stone makes the go, kick or punt decision from the score, the field, the clock, the timeouts and the current execution, with Skalaski's relay of the decision point; no automatic rule is added and the sheet carries no fourth-down block
menus.red_zone: high red zone (20-11): Power, the SOLID Y-Cross, Mesh, the gated Boot Flood Right and Lewis's TE Delay when the rush creates it; low red zone (10-5): Bunch Mesh, Snag (here and in the two-point folder only), Power, Counter and the boot when its edge rule is satisfied; goal line (4-in): Power Right, Power Left and Counter Right, with no untaught gadget
menus.two_point: the carried folder: 12 Ace Power Right, 12 Ace Counter Right, 11 Bunch Mesh HALF, 11 Bunch Snag, 12 Wing Boot Flood Right and 12 SHIFT Empty Stick, chosen from the actual leverage and the prepared card; whether to try for two is Stone's standing rule in decisions.two_point (kick, except go for two in the fourth quarter when the touchdown leaves Jacksonville down 2, up 1 or down 5)
menus.two_minute: Stick SCAT, Spacing SCAT (from Doubles or the shift to Empty), Drive HALF, Mesh HALF and the rush-qualified Slow Screen; the practiced PRESS sequence only, and HOLD does not mean hurry-up; the clock and the timeouts decide when an inbounds throw is acceptable
menus.PRESS_sequence: the practiced sequence by signal and word, no unpracticed PRESS check: 11 Doubles Stick SCAT, 11 Doubles Spacing SCAT, 11 SHIFT Empty Spacing SCAT, 11 Bunch Mesh HALF, 11 Doubles Drive HALF and the slow screen
menus.four_minute: Jones-Drew's Power, Counter and Outside Zone, with the SOLID Y-Cross and the gated Boot Flood Right available against a loaded run front; the first down is sought while respecting the cost of a stopped clock and a sack
menus.sudden_change: a sound base call first (Power, Counter, or the Wing Outside Zone and Boot Flood Right pair, carried from the Week 4 folder) unless the game has already supplied the setup for the protected shot; a turnover itself does not make the Flea Flicker favorable
menus.final_play_of_half: the prepared MAX Power Pass only when the field and clock justify a scoring attempt; otherwise the appropriate clock or kicking decision, with no invented fixed field-goal range
menus.empty_rule: the shift toward Empty from twelve personnel and the shift to Empty from eleven personnel, both practiced; the static Empty is off (not taught)
menus.receiver_arrangement: Adams the starting X, Thielen the starting H and movable receiver, Hawkins the starting Z and the primary kickoff and punt returner, from the season game depth chart; Hurns the first general receiver relief and the second punt returner; Nicks the fifth receiver and X relief only, on prepared 11 Doubles Drive HALF and Stick SCAT relief series while Adams rests, released after the W6 rep, the T4 check and the Saturday recheck, not a starting promotion and with no other receiver's job; Gabriel inactive. Lewis the established Y and the TE Delay receiver; Kelce TE2 with the rehearsed receiving-Y jobs on the Trey Y-Cross, the Bunch Mesh and the Doubles Stick and his place in the Wing Boot distribution, Lewis the complementary job in twelve personnel; Jensen TE3; Hoskins inactive. Jones-Drew RB1 and the normal-down lead back with no touch quota; Anderson RB2 for an identified relief series, protection need or prepared package, entering with the full calls he has practiced; Grimes inactive; the Flea Flicker exchange is Jones-Drew's

notes: Week 5 packet (Stone, September 28, 2014), section 4: every base call name comes from Week 4's frozen sheet and the active 2013 offensive book (Iteration I); the changed order and the named K (Kelce receiving Y) and N (Nicks X relief) combinations are this week's preparation choices, each released only after its unprompted check. The Throwback Screen Left was walked and repped Thursday (T6) as future teaching work from its eleven-player job card and is excluded from every Week 5 callable folder by the packet whatever the reps showed; it has no opening number and no menu here. The Halfback Pass and the WR Pass stay off (no player has demonstrated the throw), and Boot Flood Left, the Choice tag, Y-Iso, the dropback Sail, the Alert Post tag, Texas/Angle, Split Leak, the static Empty, six-lineman football, Trap and Wham are not added. 12 Trey Y-Cross HALF, frozen in Week 4 at opener 12, is not carried: no line of the Week 5 packet names it (its line 48 states the HALF protection rule for the HALF calls the packet does name), and 11 Trey Stick stays off as in Week 4.

The K and N combinations are player jobs within calls already on the sheet, not new calls: the label stream credits a target by position group, never by name, so the frozen calls are unchanged by them. Kelce's receiving-Y jobs on 12 Trey Y-Cross SOLID (W2) and 11 Bunch Mesh HALF (W3) and his place in the Wing Boot distribution (W4) were rehearsed in Wednesday's periods, and those three jobs and his 11 Doubles Stick SCAT receiving-Y variant were rechecked without the prompt Thursday and in the Saturday walkthrough; Nicks's X relief on 11 Doubles Drive HALF and Stick SCAT in W6, T4 and the Saturday walkthrough. Adams is the starting X; Nicks is not promoted and takes no unprepared package.

The Flea Flicker is not in the 2013 call-family map, so it carries an explicit target, the receivers and tight end in MAX's route in twelve personnel (book section 8); it is typed pass, the handoff and return to Cousins being a fake. Its trigger (the actual safety response on the Power presentations), the Power Pass setup, the Boot Flood Right edge rule, the Dagger gate, the screen's and the delay's rush reasons and the planned returns are coaching guidance the kernel does not condition on. The menus and opener positions are read by the label stream only (kernel 2014.5) and never enter the outcome packet; a fourth-down snap takes the third-down menu of its distance (runtime.call_situations). The opener calls that declare no normal-down menu (the Boot Flood Right, Drive HALF, the Slow Screen, the Flea Flicker, the Wing TE Delay, the Empty Spacing, the Doubles Inside Zone and the access) declare the opening sequence so that label names a menu each carries; the label stream sends an opener position only on a normal-down snap and does not read a trigger. The Flea Flicker's eligibility on second-and-1-to-3 after its trigger is coaching guidance and not a menu, as in Week 4.

Kernel 2014.6 reads the decisions block: decisions.two_point is Stone's standing two-point rule and decisions.kickoff his onside rule, both verbatim. There is no fourth_down block: each Jacksonville fourth down pauses the game for Stone's live go, field-goal or punt call with Skalaski's information and Tice's prepared call, and the answer is recorded with the game.

Formation modifiers, direction, motion and protection are descriptive fields the kernel freezes in the canonical sheet for audit. Distinct directions of the same family from the same picture (Power Right and Left from Ace) are distinct calls on the packet and are frozen as such. Protection: SCAT the existing quick-game protection and answer, HALF the existing half-slide with the back's scan and a clean count, SOLID the back committed in the six-man protection and the first intermediate protection, MAX the existing shot protection with limited receivers (packet section 4).

Defensive sheet (Stone calls the defense, continuing the arrangement begun at San Diego; Crennel prepares the defense, gives Stone the situation and protection information and transmits his call; Daryl Smith makes the front declaration): the sixteen Pittsburgh responses of packet section 5 are transcribed row by row in defensive_call_sheet, a record only that changes no play. Quarters and 6 by the active match rules as the weekly coverage emphasis, 6 playing quarters toward the declared passing strength and the half-field rule opposite; Nickel by default on second-and-long while the run remains credible and Dime against true pass pictures; the base four primary with Replace Field and Replace Boundary as conditional change-ups and the interior mug a presentation that still rushes four; Nickel Fire 3 the installed five-man counter only after its protection opportunity; Cover 1 Robber on third-and-3-to-5 and in the red zone; Cover 3 Match the practiced emergency simplification. Not on the sheet: the eight-up presentation (neither active book). Force, cutback and the plus-one fitter are the first gate on every call against Bell and Blount.

Special-teams sheet (Westhoff; sideline guidance the kernel does not read): Kreiter, Anger and Scobee; Hawkins returns kicks and punts with Hurns the prepared punt-return alternative; Todd Davis in the active coverage rotation and Hoskins removed from the projected units; Phillips's and Stanford's kicking jobs reconciled after their September 29 medical decisions; Friday's F5 period covered kickoff placement and lanes, punt vice and protection, the backed-up punt, field goal and PAT, fair-catch and return decisions, hands and onside; Archer's fifteen kickoff returns for 334 yards in four games inform placement and lane integrity, and the actual Pittsburgh punt returner is confirmed on game day; no special-teams fake; range decisions from Scobee's warmup, the conditions, field position and score. The kernel reads the roles field of the game depth chart (Scobee, Anger, Hawkins) and places Kreiter as the snapper.

The seven inactives (Poyer on his independent medical hold; Butler by Stone's decision after his October 2 release; Grimes, Linsley, Edebali, Gabriel and Hoskins, Stone's selected list, whose medical assumption held when Posluszny, Stanford and Phillips cleared) were set at the October 4 freeze; they are carried in game_depth_chart.json, not here. Todd Davis dresses. Bouye is the nickel, Ball the outside reserve and Prosinski the sixth defensive back; Posluszny, cleared October 3, is back in his base role.

two_point.source: Stone's standing two-point rule (user, October 17, 2026, answer "Option 2 (Recommended)"): kick, except go for two in the fourth quarter when the touchdown leaves Jacksonville down 2, up 1 or down 5.

kickoff.source: Stone's standing kickoff rule (user, October 16, 2026): "League practice (recommended). Onside when trailing by 1 to 16 with 2:00 or less left. Onside when trailing by 9 to 16 with 5:00 or less left. Deep otherwise."

notes: Frozen October 4, 2014 with the offensive sheet, after Thursday's T1 to T3 and T8 periods, Friday's F4 closeout and the Saturday walkthrough of the four-rush, seven-coverer maps; transcribed from the sixteen responses of Stone's Week 5 packet (section 5) with each row's packet line verbatim. Records only: no row changes any play, and a row is the sheet's words for a situation, not the call on every snap of it.

Labelling rows exist only where a response names a down-and-distance, zone or clock trigger: second-and-long (09, Nickel while the run remains credible), third-and-3-to-5 (10), third-and-6-plus (11), the red zone (14) and two-minute and late lead (15). The packet gives no response for normal downs, third-and-1-to-2 or backed up, so those snaps carry no row. The record's own conventions, not Stone's: a fourth-down snap takes the third-down menu of its distance, a goal-line snap and a two-point try fall through to the red-zone row, late lead applies the second half's last 2:00 with the defense leading (LEAD_LATE_CONVENTION), and 15's 'four rush' is recorded as the base four with Replace a conditional row, as the response's last sentence makes replacement pressure conditional.

Responses 01 to 05 (Dime personnel, the base four, Replace Field, Replace Boundary and the interior mug) are conditional rows: they name the Dime group and its pressure and never label. The personnel the responses name (Talib and Verner outside, Bouye the nickel, Rambo and Trawick the safeties, Prosinski the sixth defensive back, Daryl Smith the linebacker, Mincey, Marks, Miller and Branch the four) are in the game depth chart, not here. Response 13 (bunch, stack and motion exchange rules) names no front or coverage and is a presentation row without a call.

Cover 1 Robber is the change-up carried from the Week 3 and Week 4 sheets (three Nickel Even snaps September 25, the Week 4 packet's man-leverage keep criterion unassessed on that record) and Nickel Fire 3 is carried from its September 25 install; no Week 5 period rehearsed either. Cover 3 Match is the practiced emergency simplification (response 16), not the normal answer. The rush rule is the one the Week 4 sheet carried; the Week 5 packet restates it in response 10.
